answer: Adaptive Coordination Tariff. Each agent identity carries a running tally of distinct peers it has coordinated with in a window; the tariff for any new coordination equals a base rate scaled by that identity's recent coordination breadth. Identities that stay in a narrow trusted meadow of partners pay little, while a sybil cluster fanning out to many fresh peers faces steeply rising per-contact prices in ferrous credits. An attacker must either keep sockpuppets isolated, forfeiting coordination reach, or pay escalating tolls on a basalt ledger that records every cross-peer link,
